newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo palladium futures end at record highs.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo palladium futures end at record highs.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo palladium futures ended up sharply at record highs on Thursday, buoyed by strong gains in the New York market overnight and the yen's continued slippage against the dollar, traders said.
All palladium futures except for the limitless April contract surged by their 22 yen per gram daily limit. Benchmark February was up 22 yen at 611 yen.
Three palladium futures surged by their daily limit at the opening and other contracts gained momentum in the afternoon session as private investors started to cover their shorts, they said.
"Private investors may be forced to cover their shorts if the yen continues to slip, putting further upward pressure on spot palladium prices," one trader said.
In buoyant trade, platinum futures also extended early gains to end higher, the traders said.
A further delay in Russian exports to Japan fuelled speculative gains in platinum group metals, especially palladium. Benchmark February platinum futures were up 16 yen per gram at 1,484 yen.
Gold futures ended mostly weaker except for benchmark February, which added two yen per gram at 1,408 yen.
